heading: Agent
text: Run an approved plan with live requests that ask for your approval.Agentmode runs an approved plan against the target. Every live request asks for Approve / Deny unless you enable batch approvals. The composer placeholder reads Ask the agent to run the plan…

heading: Before you start
text: Finish a Plan document and build/approve the campaign kit in Library.Set Target scope.Pick a model with a configured key.Finish or stop any current chat turn. Pilot note Some pilot builds temporarily disable Agent or Explore. If you see that message, try again later or use Ask / Plan.

heading: Run
text: Start attack From the plan-ready prompt, start the attack. Approve requests Each live send shows Allow this request?with Deny, Stopand Allow. See Approvals & stop. Watch progress Status lines like Calling model…and tool activity appear in the thread. Findings with evidence go to Records. Stop attackends the run. Skip endpoint/ Retryappear when a step fails.

heading: Approvals & stop
text: Approve live requests, stop runs, Explore toggles and spend caps.When Agent (or Explore) is about to send live traffic or spend tokens, PentAgent asks first.

heading: Allow this request?
text: The prompt shows a short summary and about how many requests. Choose: Button What it does Deny Blocks this send. Stop Stops everything for the run. Allow Lets this request through. Under AI models, you can enable Approve batch (one Allow for following sends)so one Allow covers the rest of that attack until you Stop.

heading: Explore (per mode)
text: In AI settings, each mode (Ask / Plan / Agent) has an Explore toggle. When off, that mode only uses endpoints you drop into chat. When on, a whole-app explore shows a cost warning first if Warn about cost before exploringis enabled. Destructive actions get their own prompt.

heading: Spend cap
text: Spend caps are off by default — PentAgent does not sell models. Under AI models you can turn on Enforce spend / token limitsand set session / daily money or token limits. Chat stops cleanly when a cap is hit. Money caps need a provider that reports cost; token caps use provider usage when available.

heading: Stop
text: Use Stopon the approval prompt, Stop attackin the thread, or the Stop control in the composer to halt a run.

heading: Ask
text: Ask questions about traffic, scope and coverage in the AI Assistant.Askis the default mode of the AI Assistantpanel. Use it to ask about captured traffic, scope and coverage. It doesn’t run attacks.

heading: Open the assistant
text: The assistant docks on the right. Toggle it with, open the chat list, or go fullscreen with the fullscreen control. Pick a Modeand Modelin the composer. If no models are configured, set them under AI models.

heading: Chat
text: Type in the composer (Ask about traffic, scope, coverage…) and send.+ Newstarts a new chat. Delete chats from the list.Copy a response with the copy control on the message.Drop a request into chat (or select one) so Contextfills. Open Inspectorshows the message.Explore for Ask mode can be turned off in Settings. When it’s on and a whole-app explore would run, you get a cost warning first. See Approvals & stop.

heading: Context
text: Attach recon notes and see the request selected for the assistant.Context has two sides: the request currently selected for chat, and your own recon notes attached to the project.

heading: Selected request
text: In the AI Assistant, the Contextstrip shows the selected message. Select a request to populate context.Open Inspectoropens the full breakdown. Status for the selection is listed under Status.

heading: Context notes
text: The Context notespanel (project context) lets you attach recon output, business profile and roles. Field Use ScopeProjector Host.Host When scope is Host, the hostname the notes apply to. Title A short label. Notes (markdown) Paste recon output, business profile, roles… Click Save contextto keep the notes with the project.

heading: Plan
text: Write an attack plan the agent can follow.Planmode writes a named guide on the left (types and library paths, not full payload dumps). Edit it there anytime. The composer placeholder reads Describe what to test…

heading: Write a plan
text: Switch to Plan Choose Planin the mode dropdown. Switching to Plan disarms Agent until you Start attack. Describe what to test Answer clarifying questions if the assistant asks them (including Otherwith a free-text answer). Review the plan on the left Use Open on left/ Viewing on left. Edit the document directly. Build the kit When the plan is ready, build and approve a campaign kit in Kits. Set Target scope before you Start attack from Agent. The assistant will remind you if scope is empty.

heading: HTTP history
text: Browse, search and filter everything the proxy has captured.Proxy › HTTP historylists every request and response that went through the listener for the current project, newest first. Rows appear live while you browse in the lab window.

heading: The list
text: The toolbar: HTTP/ HTTPSchips, a Domainpicker, Search requests…, the Filterbutton and the count of matching rows.The table. By default it shows #, Method, URL, Status code, Length, Timeand Source.The selected exchange, with the request on one side and the response on the other.Long histories load in pages. The line above the table reads Showing 50 of 1,240 (newest first)or similar. Click Load more rowsto fetch more.

heading: Look at a request
text: Click a row to open it below the table. Each side has pretty, rawand hexviews. From here you can: Click the Send to Repeaterarrow to open the request in Repeaterand switch to it.Right-click the row or the message for more actions, like sending it to other tools.The Inspectorpanel on the right breaks the selected message into params, cookies and headers.

heading: Search and filter
text: Type in Search requests…to narrow the list. A small ×clears it. The HTTPand HTTPSchips and the Domainpicker are quick toggles. Click a chip again to turn it off.

heading: The filter dialog
text: Click Filterfor everything else.Quick filters: the same protocol and domain choices as the toolbar.History filters: host, method, status, status class, path/URL search, and the hide options below.Columns: pick which columns the table shows. Filter Default Hide static On. Hides CSS, scripts, images and fonts. Hide browser noise On. Hides browser telemetry, updates and connectivity checks. Hide CDN On. Hides common CDN hosts. All hosts/ In scope/ Out of scopeIn scope, unless your project options say otherwise.Legacy extension traffic Off. Only for rows captured by an older browser extension. Seeing fewer rows than you expect? History starts filtered to in-scope hosts. If your project has no scope yet, or the site you’re browsing isn’t in it, switch the scope filter to All hosts, or add the host on the Targettab.

heading: Filtering to one host
text: Some views, like the insights strip under the history, can narrow the list to one host. A Host: demo.localline then appears above the toolbar. Click clearto remove it.

heading: Clear history
text: In the filter dialog, Clear historydeletes every captured request for this project. PentAgent asks you to confirm first, because this can’t be undone. Refreshreloads the list.

heading: When the list is empty
text: With no captures yet, the sub-tab shows the Get your first capturesteps. See First run, then browse your target in the lab window.

heading: Import
text: Bring in HAR or XML captures, and move whole projects between machines.Proxy › Importhas two jobs: adding traffic you captured somewhere else to this project, and moving a whole project in or out as one file. Import a traffic file into this project.Portable engagement: export or import a whole project.

heading: Import traffic
text: PentAgent reads.harfiles saved from Chrome or Firefox developer tools, and XML exports from other intercepting proxies. Choose a file Click the box that reads Choose HAR or proxy XML fileand pick your file. Wait for the import The box shows Importing…. Each entry becomes a row in HTTP history and a node in the sitemap. Bigger files import in the background. You’ll see Import started — track progress on the Dashboard, and the progress shows on the Dashboardtab.

heading: Move a whole project
text: A.pentagent.zipholds a project’s traffic, Intruder setups, scope and settings. Export engagementdownloads the current project as one file.Import engagement zipadds the file as a brand-new project. Pick it from the project picker afterwards. Your current project isn’t changed. Exports are handy for handing work to a teammate, or for keeping a copy before you clear history.

heading: Match / Replace
text: Rewrite requests and responses automatically as they pass through.Proxy › Match / Replacerules change traffic automatically. They run while the listener captures, before anything reaches Intercept or HTTP history. Use them to swap a header, flip a flag in a URL, or tidy up a response body without stopping each request by hand. The form for a new rule.Your rules. Each one has an onbox and a Deletebutton.

heading: Add a rule
text: Name it Give the rule a short Nameso you can spot it later. Pick where it applies Choose Request, Responseor Both, then the part to look in. Fill in Match and Replace Leave Replaceempty to remove what matched. Tick Regexto use a regular expression. Click Add rule The rule is on straight away. Where Looks in Any The URL, headers and body. URL The request URL only. Headers The header lines. Body The message body. In the list, a rule shows as match → replacewith where it applies, for example request/headers · regex. An empty replace shows as ∅.

heading: Turn a rule off or delete it
text: Untick onto pause a rule without losing it. Deleteremoves it for good.Rules belong to the current project, so each project can have its own set. Rules only change traffic captured from now on. Requests already in HTTP history stay as they were.

heading: Proxy & Intercept
text: Start capturing, then pause, edit, forward or drop requests with Intercept.The Proxytab is where traffic from the lab browser comes in. It has five sub-tabs: Intercept, HTTP history, WebSockets, Match / Replaceand Import. This page covers the listener and the Interceptsub-tab.

heading: Start and stop the listener
text: PentAgent captures through a local listener, 127.0.0.1:8088by default. You can start it from any of these places: The proxy button in the top bar. It reads Proxy Offuntil the listener runs.Start proxyin the Get your first capturesteps.Open lab browser, which starts the listener for you if it isn’t running.To stop, click the proxy button again (its tooltip reads Stop proxy (127.0.0.1:8088)), use the ■next to Labat the bottom of the left menu, or Stop listenerin Settings › Proxy & gateway. Once it stops, the lab browser shows No internetuntil you open it again. The listener belongs to one project at a time. If another project is using it, the Proxy tab says Listener owned by another project. Opening the lab browser or turning on Intercept here moves it to this project.

heading: Intercept
text: Intercept pauses matching traffic in the lab browser so you can look at it, change it, and then send it on or drop it. While Intercept is off, traffic flows normally and shows up in HTTP history. The Intercept is off/ Intercept is onswitch.What to pause, and what to let through without stopping.Intercept match rulesfor finer control.

heading: Turn Intercept on
text: Click Intercept is off It turns into Intercept is on. If the listener isn’t capturing yet, PentAgent starts it and opens the lab browser if needed. Your everyday browser isn’t affected. Reload your target in the lab window The page waits while its requests are held. Static files like CSS, scripts, images and fonts are skipped by default. Turning Intercept off again forwards everything still in the queue, so nothing is left hanging.

heading: Choose what gets paused
text: Option What it does Intercept requests Pause requests on their way to the site. Intercept responses Pause responses on their way back to the browser. Don't intercept static (css/js/images/fonts) Let page assets through without stopping. Don't intercept browser noise Skip browser telemetry, updates, connectivity checks and prefetch. In-scope onlyOnly pause traffic to hosts in your project’s scope. On unless you turn it off.Intercept WebSocket frames Pause WebSocket messages as well as HTTP.

heading: Intercept match rules
text: Rules sit on top of the options above. Click Add rule, pick Includeor Exclude, then choose what to match on: Host, Method, Path, URL, Headeror Protocol(httpor websocket). Each rule has its own on/off box. If any include rule is on, traffic has to match at least one include to be paused.An exclude rule always wins over an include.

heading: Work through held items
text: The queue, with Forward alland Drop allabove it. The sub-tab shows a count, like Intercept (2).Actions for the selected item.The editor. Change the method, URL, headers or body. For a response, you can change the status, headers and body. Action What happens Forward Sends the item on, with any edits you made. Forward & next Sends it on and stays ready to pause the next matching item. Drop Throws the item away. The browser never gets it. The keyboard shortcuts work when the Intercept panel has focus. Click anywhere inside it first.

heading: If something doesn’t work
text: What you see What to try Intercept is on but lab Chromium is not running Open the lab browser (Labin the left menu, or Settings › Proxy & gateway), then reload the target there. Nothing gets paused Check that you’re browsing in the lab window, and that the host is in scope or In-scope onlyis off. Pages stall after you leave Intercept on Turn Intercept off. The queue is forwarded automatically.

heading: WebSockets
text: See WebSocket frames captured through the proxy.When a site opens a WebSocket through the lab browser, PentAgent records each frame. You’ll find them on Proxy › WebSockets.

heading: Frames
text: The frame list: Dir(→ sent, ← received), Type, Host / pathand Time.The payload of the selected frame. Text frames show as plain text, binary frames as base64.The list updates live while the connection is open.

heading: Pause frames with Intercept
text: To stop frames and change them before they go through, turn on Intercept WebSocket frameson the Interceptsub-tab. You can also write an intercept match rule on Protocolwith the value websocket. Seeing No WebSocket frames yet? The site you’re on may not use WebSockets, or you may be browsing outside the lab window.

heading: Records
text: The engagement report in Markdown, with chapters you or the model can maintain.Recordsis the client-facing engagement report for the current project. Chapters are written and maintained by the model by default; you can edit any of them anytime. Confirmed findings with evidence from Scanner and Agent also land here.

heading: When it’s empty
text: With nothing written yet you’ll see No reports yet. You can Seed draft chapters, Open Agentto start testing, or Write manually.

heading: Work with chapters
text: Action What it does Refresh LLM drafts Regenerates unlocked chapters from current project facts. Copy markdown Copies the whole report to the clipboard. Edit markdown Edit a chapter yourself. It becomes locked so the model won't overwrite it. Unlock for LLM Lets the model maintain that chapter again. Each chapter shows whether it is Edited by youor Maintained by LLM, and when it was last updated. Scope for the project is listed under Project scope.

heading: First run
text: Create a project, start the proxy, and capture your first request.Once you’re past the welcome screen, PentAgent opens its main window. This page walks through the window and gets your first request captured.

heading: The main window
text: Projectpicker. Switch between your projects here.New projectfield and its +button.The proxy button. It reads Proxy Offuntil you start capturing, and turns on once a project is open.The left menu, grouped into Workbench, Projectand AI Agent.Your workspace, with the Proxy, Repeater, Intruderand Scannertabs on top.Inspector, which shows params, cookies and headers for the message you select.AI Assistant, with Ask, Plan and Agent modes.The listener strip: whether the proxy is listening, plus Laband Settingsshortcuts.

heading: Create a project
text: A project keeps everything for one app together: its traffic, scope, findings and AI chats. Type a name in the New projectfield in the top bar and press Enteror click +. The new project opens straight away. Next, click the Targetbutton next to the project name. It opens the Targettab, where you add your app’s host to the project’s scope. Until you do, the button reads No scope hosts.

heading: Get your first capture
text: With a project open, the Dashboardshows a short Get your first capturechecklist. The next step to do is highlighted, and finished steps get a tick. Start proxy Click Start proxy. PentAgent starts a listener on 127.0.0.1:8088that records the traffic passing through it. The step then reads Listening 127.0.0.1:8088. CA certificate To read HTTPS traffic, the browser needs to trust PentAgent’s certificate. PentAgent creates its local PentAgent CAcertificate on your computer and the lab browser trusts it automatically, so usually there’s nothing to do here. Download CAsaves the certificate as pentagent-ca-cert.crt. You only need it if you want to send traffic from another browser or tool through PentAgent yourself. Open lab browser Click Open lab browser. A separate Chromium window opens, already connected to the proxy. It has its own profile, so your everyday browser, its logins and its history are never involved. It starts on example.com. First capture In the lab window, go to the app you’re testing and click around. Each request appears in Proxy› HTTP history. Once the first one arrives, the checklist steps aside. Only test apps you own or have permission to test. A practice app running on your own computer, such as OWASP Juice Shop, is a good place to start.

heading: The same steps in the Proxy tab
text: You’ll find the same checklist, in a compact form, in Proxy› HTTP historywhile it’s still empty.

heading: The top bar
text: Projectpicker.Targetshows your project’s scope host and opens the Target tab.Proxy button. Click it to start or stop the listener. It reads Proxy Activewhile capturing.Activityopens the Dashboard.Records, where findings and notes collect.Settings.Your account menu. See Your account menu.

heading: Changing the proxy port
text: PentAgent listens on port 8088by default. If another program already uses it, open Settings› Proxy & gatewayand change Listen portunder Listener defaults. Check porttells you whether the new port is free.

heading: If something doesn’t work
text: What you see What to do No lab browser found Restart PentAgent while connected to the internet so first-launch setup can finish downloading the lab browser. The proxy won't start Another program may be using port 8088. Pick a different Listen port in Settings › Proxy & gateway. Pages show a certificate warning Make sure you're browsing in the lab window, which trusts the PentAgent CA certificate automatically. Nothing appears in HTTP history Check the proxy button reads Proxy Active and that you're browsing in the lab window, not your everyday browser.

heading: Install
text: Download the pilot build, start it, and open PentAgent.

heading: What you need
text: Windows (64-bit), macOS (Apple Silicon), or Linux (64-bit).PentAgent bundles its own Python runtime inside the desktop app, so you don’t need to install Python yourself. An internet connectionfor the first launch, which sets up PentAgent’s private environment and downloads the isolated lab browser. About 2 GB of free disk spacefor the app, its local environment, and the lab browser. Pilot access.Anyone can download the build, but signing in needs an approved pilot account. If you haven’t applied yet, request pilot access.

heading: Download the pilot build
text: Open the download page Go to Downloadand pick the package for your operating system. Verify the checksum (optional) Each build has a matching.sha256file next to it. In the folder where you saved both files, you can verify the download: # Windows (PowerShell) Get-FileHash.\PentAgent-win-x64.zip -Algorithm SHA256 # macOS shasum -a 256 -c PentAgent-mac-arm64.dmg.sha256 # Linux sha256sum -c pentagent_amd64.deb.sha256

heading: Windows (64-bit)
text: Extract the archive Right-click PentAgent-win-x64.zipand choose Extract All…to unpack it into a normal folder on your disk (for example C:\Users\<you>\PentAgent). Don’t run the app from inside the zip preview window. Start PentAgent Open the extracted win-unpackedfolder and double-click pentagent.exe. If Windows SmartScreen shows Windows protected your PC, click More infoand then Run anyway.

heading: macOS (Apple Silicon)
text: Move PentAgent to Applications Open PentAgent-mac-arm64.dmgand drag PentAgentinto Applications(or unpack PentAgent-mac-arm64.zipand move PentAgent.appinto Applications). Open the app the first time Pilot builds are ad-hoc signed rather than Apple-notarized. For the first launch, open Applications, right-click(or Control-click) PentAgentand choose Open, then click Openin the dialog (or allow it under System Settings › Privacy & Security › Open Anyway). If macOS still blocks the app after a browser download, clear the quarantine attribute in Terminal and open it again: xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/PentAgent.app

heading: Linux (64-bit)
text: Pick whichever package fits your distribution:Debian, Ubuntu, Kali, or Linux Mint (.deb): sudo apt install./pentagent_amd64.deb pentagent AppImage (portable single file): chmod +x PentAgent-linux-x86_64.AppImage./PentAgent-linux-x86_64.AppImage Portable tarball (.tar.gz): tar xzf pentagent-linux-x64.tar.gz./pentagent-*/pentagent

heading: What happens on the first launch
text: The first time you open PentAgent, the startup screen prepares a private Python environment and downloads an isolated Chromium lab browser so your everyday browser is never touched. This takes a few minutes over a normal internet connection. Later launches skip setup and open in a few seconds. PentAgent’s engine and proxy listen only on 127.0.0.1(your own computer), so nobody else on your network can reach them.

heading: Starting and quitting
text: Launch PentAgent from your applications menu, Dock, or folder. To quit cleanly and stop the background engine, close the PentAgent window or press (on macOS).

heading: Where your data lives
text: PentAgent stores its environment, local CA certificate, and project database in your user data folder:Windows:%LOCALAPPDATA%\PentAgentmacOS:~/Library/Application Support/PentAgentLinux:~/.local/share/pentagent

heading: Launch options
text: Most people never need these. You can set them as environment variables before starting PentAgent: Launch options PENTAGENT_PORT Pin a specific local port for the PentAgent engine instead of picking a free port automatically. Automatic You want the local engine on a fixed port. PENTAGENT_DATA Override the folder for PentAgent's Python environment, certificates, and project database. OS data folder You'd like PentAgent's data on a different disk or folder.

heading: Updating to a new build
text: Quit PentAgent Close PentAgent so the local engine stops cleanly. Install the new build Download the latest package from Downloadand replace your previous app folder or package. Open PentAgent Start the new build. Your project database stays in your PentAgent data folder, so your projects and history are ready when the new version opens. If PentAgent says Update requiredwhen you sign in, your build is older than the pilot supports. See Update required.

heading: Uninstalling
text: To remove PentAgent completely:Quit PentAgent.Remove the application (delete the extracted folder on Windows, drag PentAgent.appto Trash on macOS, or run sudo apt remove pentagent/ delete the AppImage or tarball folder on Linux). Delete your PentAgent data folder (%LOCALAPPDATA%\PentAgenton Windows, ~/Library/Application Support/PentAgenton macOS, or ~/.local/share/pentagentand ~/.cache/ms-playwrighton Linux). This removes the Python environment, project database, lab browser profile, and local CA files. If you imported the PentAgent CAcertificate into your system or browser trust store for manual proxy setups, remove PentAgent CAfrom your trust store as well.

heading: First-launch setup didn’t finish
text: Check your internet connection and click Try againon the startup screen. If setup stopped halfway through creating the environment, delete the venvfolder inside your PentAgent data folder and open PentAgent again so it sets up cleanly from scratch.

heading: Checking the logs
text: Choose Help › Show Logsfrom the PentAgent menu bar (or click Show Logson the startup screen) to open the folder containing backend.logand desktop.log.

heading: Getting started
text: The short path from download to your first captured request.Getting set up takes four short steps. Each one has its own guide if you want more detail.

heading: Before you begin
text: An approved pilot request. If you don’t have one yet, request pilot access. The GitHub account you used on your request.A 64-bit Windows, macOS (Apple Silicon), or 64-bit Linux computer with an internet connection for the first launch. An app you own or have permission to test. A practice app on your own machine works well.

heading: The quick path
text: Install PentAgent Download the pilot build for Windows, macOS, or Linux and open PentAgent. The first launch sets up the local engine and lab browser for you. Install Sign in with GitHub PentAgent checks that your account is approved for the pilot. Sign in Tick two boxes Agree to the Terms and Privacy Policy, and confirm you’ll only test apps you’re allowed to. You only do this once. Welcome screen Capture your first request Create a project, start the proxy, open the lab browser and visit your app. Requests show up as you browse. First run Everything stays on your computer The traffic you capture and the projects you create are stored locally. Our servers only see your account check and anonymous usage analytics. When you use the AI features, requests go to the model you choose.

heading: Sign in
text: Sign in with GitHub and what happens while your access is being approved.PentAgent asks you to sign in each time it can’t find a saved session, for example on the first launch or after you sign out. Signing in lets PentAgent confirm that your account is part of the pilot.

heading: Sign in with GitHub
text: Choose Continue with GitHub Click Continue with GitHub. The button changes to Redirecting…while GitHub opens. Approve on GitHub Sign in to GitHub if you aren’t already, and approve PentAgent. Use the GitHub account from your pilot request, since that’s the one on the approved list. Back to PentAgent GitHub sends you back to PentAgent, which checks your access. If you’re approved and it’s your first time, you’ll see the welcome screen next. After that, PentAgent opens straight to your workspace. What PentAgent gets from GitHub Your name, GitHub username, email address and profile picture. PentAgent uses them to check your access and to show who’s signed in. It doesn’t ask for access to your repositories. Email sign-in is coming soon Signing in with a one-time code sent to your email is on its way. For now, use GitHub.

heading: How access checks work
text: Right after you sign in, PentAgent asks our server whether your account is on the pilot list. It checks again every few hours while the app is open, and whenever you come back to the PentAgent window. If you lose your internet connection, you can keep working. As long as PentAgent confirmed your access on this computer within the last three days, it lets you in with the same account.

heading: If your access isn’t approved yet
text: If your account isn’t on the pilot list yet, PentAgent shows Not approved yetwith the GitHub username it checked. What you can do:Haven’t applied yet?Click Apply for pilot accessto open the pilot request form. Already applied?We review requests by hand, so it can take a little while. Once you’re approved, open PentAgent again and you’ll go straight in. Signed in with a different GitHub account?Click Sign outand sign in with the account from your request.

heading: Could not verify pilot access
text: PentAgent couldn’t reach our server to check your access, and there’s no recent confirmation on this computer to fall back on. Check your connection, then click Try again. You can also Sign outfrom here.

heading: Update required
text: Your build is older than the oldest version the pilot supports. Click Get the latest build, then follow Updating to a new build. When a newer build is out but yours still works, PentAgent shows a small Update availablebar at the top of the window instead. It has a Downloadlink and a Dismissbutton, so you can update when it suits you.

heading: Your account menu
text: Once you’re in, your account button sits at the far right of the top bar. It shows your GitHub profile picture, or your initials if you don’t have one. Click it to see your account details. Your name and GitHub username.The email address on your GitHub account.Your access status, for example Pilot access · allowed. Sign out. The menu only ever shows your own details. Press Escor click anywhere else to close it.

heading: Signing out
text: Open the account menu and click Sign out. PentAgent returns to the sign-in screen. Your projects and captured traffic stay on your computer and are there when you sign in again.

heading: If sign-in doesn’t work
text: What you see What to do GitHub opens but you never get back to PentAgent Close the GitHub tab, go back to PentAgent and click Continue with GitHub again. Make sure you finish the approval on GitHub. Not approved yet, but you were approved Check you signed in with the GitHub account from your pilot request. If it's the right one, sign out and sign in again. Could not verify pilot access Check your internet connection, then click Try again.

heading: Welcome screen
text: The two quick checkboxes you see once, before the app opens.The first time you sign in, PentAgent shows a short welcome screen before the app opens. It asks for two things, and you only need to do it once.

heading: What’s on the screen
text: I agree to the Terms and Privacy Policy.The two links open the Terms and Privacy Policyon our website, so you can read them first. I’ll only test apps I own or have permission to test.A simple promise that keeps everyone safe. Includes anonymous usage analytics.The link opens the analytics sectionof the Privacy Policy. The versions of the Terms and Privacy Policy you’re agreeing to.Continuebecomes available once both boxes are ticked.

heading: Tick both boxes and continue
text: Tick both boxes and click Continue. The button shows Saving…for a moment while PentAgent records your choice on your account, then the app opens. Prefer to stop here? Click Sign out. Nothing is saved, and you’ll see this screen again next time you sign in.

heading: About analytics
text: PentAgent sends anonymous usage analytics, such as which features get used, to help us improve it. Analytics only start once you’ve clicked Continue. Nothing is sent from the sign-in or welcome screens. Your captured traffic stays on your computer. The Privacy Policyexplains exactly what is and isn’t collected.

heading: When you’ll see it again
text: Your answer is saved to your account, not just this computer, so signing in elsewhere won’t ask again. You’ll only see the welcome screen again if we publish a new version of the Terms or the Privacy Policy. In that case, have a quick look at what changed and tick the boxes again.

heading: If it doesn’t work
text: If PentAgent can’t load the current Terms and Privacy versions, it shows We couldn’t load the latest termswith a Try againbutton instead of the checkboxes. Here’s what each message means: Message What to do You're offline. Reconnect and try again. Check your internet connection, then click Try again. We couldn't reach PentAgent just now. Try again in a moment. Wait a moment, then click Try again. We're still setting things up on our side. Try again a little later. Nothing's wrong on your end. Try again a little later. We couldn't save that. Check your connection and try again. Check your connection, then click Try again. That didn't save. Please try again. Click Try again. The Terms or Privacy Policy just changed. Have a quick look and tick the boxes again. A new version came out while the screen was open. Read it, tick both boxes and continue. You've been signed out. Sign in again to continue. Sign in again with GitHub. PentAgent only opens once your choice is safely saved, so if a message appears you’ll stay on this screen until it works.

heading: Introduction
text: DocsPentAgent documentation PentAgent is a desktop workbench for testing web apps. It captures traffic through a local proxy, helps you understand what it sees, and only runs tests when you say so. These guides walk through every part of it. New here? Start with Getting started. It takes you from download to your first captured request in a few minutes. Overview

heading: Testing responsibly
text: Only test apps you own or have permission to test. A practice app running on your own machine is a great place to start.

heading: Dashboard
text: See capture health, findings, scans and recent evidence for the current project.The Dashboardis the overview for the current project. Open it from the left menu under Project. With no project selected it says Open or create a project to see capture health, findings, and recent evidence.

heading: What you see
text: Card What it shows CaptureProxy status, transaction count and last seen. Open history/ See historyjumps to HTTP history. If the proxy is off, it points you to start it.UnderstandingHosts, pages and tech from the Target map. Open Target →opens the sitemap.FindingsIssues from passive scans. Open Scanner, or Run a passive scan/ Launch passive scanwhen empty.TestingScan runs and other tasks. New scan/ Start a passive scanstarts one. Double-click a task to rename it.Recent evidence Jump points to transactions linked from scan issues. Background imports and kit builds also show progress here under other tasks.

heading: Kits
text: Browse the attack library and build campaign kits from Plan threads.Kits(the Library pane) holds the seed library of skills and suites, plus campaign kits you build from a Plan thread.

heading: Seed library
text: Pick a skill or suite in the tree to preview methodology text. The seed library is a read-only reference: payloads and notes you can learn from. Use Enable all/ Disable allwhen editing which suites are active in a kit.

heading: Campaign kit
text: Open a Plan thread In the AI Assistant, switch to Planand work until a plan document appears on the left. Build kit from plan Click Build kit from plan(or Build campaign kitfrom the chat). Status moves from Starting kit build…to Kit ready. Review and approve Open the kit in Library, check the endpoint map (On / Parent / Param / Suites), then Approve kit. Authz plans need at least two principals before Approve / Start. Start attack Back in Agent mode, start the attack. See Agent. Open planjumps back to the Plan thread. Without a plan thread, the pane says to open one first.

heading: Sitemap
text: The Target sitemap and the UI Map built from the lab browser.PentAgent has two maps. The HTTP sitemap lives on the Targettab. The Sitemapitem in the left menu opens the Target Map(also called the UI Map) — pages and controls discovered by the lab browser extension.

heading: HTTP sitemap (Target)
text: See Target & scope → Sitemap. It fills from proxy traffic and supports in-scope / hide-static filters and send-to-Repeater.

heading: UI Map (Target Map)
text: The UI Map is separate from HTTP history. Proxy traffic alone does not create pages or buttons — only the lab browser extension does. Open it with the project selected, enter a Target URL, set Proxy mode(Off (fast explore), Optional, or Required (MITM)), then click Open lab browser. Browse only in that window; the map updates live. Control What it does Refresh map Reload pages, controls and action evidence packs. Clear map & history Deletes UI map data and HTTP history for this project (asks first). Exploration Journeys from Exploration feed UI→HTTP bindings after a rebuild. Repeat under proxy ×3 Replays a selected flow through the MITM listener. Send to Chat / Pin to plan Share a flow with the AI assistant or pin it to a plan. If the project already has proxy traffic but zero mapped pages, open the lab browser while this project is selected so the extension is seeded with the project ID, then browse in lab Chromium — not your everyday Chrome.

heading: FAQ
text: Short answers to common questions about the pilot.

heading: What is PentAgent?
text: A local workbench for authorised web testing: capture traffic through a lab browser, repeat and fuzz requests, and optionally use an AI assistant with your own model keys.

heading: Who can use the pilot?
text: Approved pilot participants who sign in with GitHub. See Sign in.

heading: Where does my data live?
text: Traffic, projects and chats stay on your machine under the pilot data directory. AI features send the context you select to the provider you configure — PentAgent doesn’t mask secrets in that traffic. Analytics only run after you accept the welcome screen; details are on the privacy page.

heading: Is this a drop-in replacement for other proxy tools?
text: No. Workflows will feel familiar if you’ve used intercepting proxies before, but labels, tabs and behaviour are PentAgent’s own. Don’t expect every feature from other tools to exist here.

heading: What about the History and Logger items?
text: Proxy › HTTP history is the main capture list. Separate History / Logger panes exist for tool-sourced traffic and exports (CSV, JSON, HAR). Prefer Proxy › HTTP history for everyday capture review.

heading: Where are Findings?
text: There isn’t a top-level Findings tab. Passive issues live under Scanner; confirmed findings and the engagement report live under Records.

heading: Shortcuts
text: Keyboard shortcuts for the workbench, Repeater and Intruder.Open the shortcut list anytime with the keyboard-shortcuts command, or from the command palette ( — command palette; docs search uses the same chord on the website).

heading: Global
text: Keys Action Open command palette? Show keyboard shortcuts Toggle Inspector Toggle Chat sidebar / dock Agent

heading: Workbench
text: Keys / gesture Action Forward selected intercept (Proxy) Drop selected intercept Forward and intercept next Right-click row Send to Repeater / Intruder / Chat / Organizer / Comparer / Decoder Double-click table row Select row and open detail pane Double-click Repeater tab Rename tab Double-click Dashboard task Rename task

heading: Repeater
text: Keys Action Send request Send without updating Content-Length New Repeater tab Close Repeater tab

heading: Intruder
text: Keys Action Start / stop attack Save attack config Add payload position (wrap selection in §…§) Exact chords can vary slightly by OS. The in-app Keyboard shortcutsdialog is the source of truth for your build.

heading: Troubleshooting
text: Fixes for common install, sign-in, proxy and capture problems.

heading: Install and launch
text: Problem What to try Windows SmartScreen or macOS Gatekeeper prompt On Windows, click More info → Run anyway. On macOS, right-click PentAgent in Applications and choose Open (see Install). Lab browser missing Restart PentAgent with an internet connection so the startup screen can finish downloading the isolated lab Chromium browser. Port already in use Change the listen port in Settings › Proxy & gateway, or stop whatever is using port 8088.

heading: Sign-in
text: Problem What to try GitHub sign-in never returns to the app Make sure you finished approving on GitHub and allowed your browser to open the pentagent:// link. Not approved yet Apply for pilot access, then wait for approval. The app rechecks every few hours. Update required Download the latest pilot build and replace your install.

heading: Capture
text: Problem What to try No rows in HTTP history Browse in the lab window, not daily Chrome. Check the history scope filter isn't hiding everything — see HTTP history. Certificate warnings Use lab Chromium (PentAgent CA is auto-trusted), or download pentagent-ca-cert.crt for a manual setup. Intercept on but nothing pauses Confirm lab Chromium is running and the host is in scope (or turn off In-scope only). UI Map empty despite proxy traffic Open the lab browser while the project is selected, then browse in that window so the extension is seeded.

heading: AI assistant
text: Problem What to try No models / provider dropdown empty Configure a provider under AI modelsand Save. Agent or Explore disabled Some pilot builds turn these off temporarily — use Ask / Plan until they're back. Spend cap hit Raise or clear limits under AI models, or wait for the daily window to reset.

heading: AI models
text: Providers, Explore toggles, approvals batch mode and spend caps.AI modelsis where you configure providers and defaults. The default provider is only what you pick here and Save — it is not inferred from.env. Existing chats keep their own provider until you change the chat dropdown.

heading: Privacy
text: Your chosen model sees raw captured traffic and chat context, including any secrets in it. PentAgent does not mask them. That provider is the only place those values go for AI features.

heading: Providers
text: Enable a provider, paste an API key (leave blank to keep a saved key), set Base URL when needed, Fetch models, Test connection, and optionally Set as default. Then Save AI settings. Model routing can be Manual, Auto (this API), or Auto (all APIs).

heading: Explore, approvals and spend caps
text: See Approvals & stopfor Explore per mode, cost warnings, batch Allow, and session / daily money and token limits. API usage for the last period is listed when providers report cost.

heading: Collaborator
text: Out-of-band listener status and environment variables.Settings for the OOB callback listener used by the Collaboratortab. Host and ports come from server.env— restart the API after changes. Control What it does Status / Domain / HTTP / DNS Shows whether the listener is up and on which ports. Start listener / Stop listener Control the local listener. Refresh Reload status. Environment variables: COLLABORATOR_LISTEN_HOST(default 127.0.0.1), COLLABORATOR_LISTEN_PORT(8099), COLLABORATOR_DNS_PORT(5300), COLLABORATOR_DOMAIN(oast.pentagent.local).

heading: General
text: Theme, API health, embeddings and lab browser overview.Open Settings from the gear in the top bar. Generalcovers appearance, server health and feature status. Section What you set Appearance Theme for the workbench. System follows your OS preference. API Status and version of the local engine. Embeddings (AI search) Whether local semantic search is active or using the lightweight keyword fallback. Server config Active local host, proxy listener defaults, and storage status. Lab browser Lists available lab browsers and notes that the capture extension loads automatically in lab Chromium. PentAgent downloads its isolated lab Chromium automatically on the first launch. If a network interruption skipped that step, restart PentAgent with an internet connection — see Install.

heading: Lab browser
text: How lab Chromium, the capture extension and proxy modes work.PentAgent launches dedicated Playwright Chromium with the capture extension — not your daily Chrome or Brave profile. Most controls live under Proxy & gateway; the overview also appears under General. Topic Details Opening Open lab browser/ Open lab Chromiumfrom onboarding, Settings, or the Labcontrol in the left menu. Extension Pre-loaded on open. Project ID and API base are set automatically. Manual options are in the extension popup. Proxy modes Required— MITM capture. Optional— MITM if the gateway is running. Off— extension-only capture, no MITM (fast explore). CA The PentAgent CA is auto-trusted in the lab profile.

heading: Project
text: Scope, rename, filter defaults, upstream proxy and delete for the active project.Projectsettings apply to the project selected in the header. Match / Replace and Import live under the Proxy tab. Section What you set Target scopeOne origin per line, templates like localhost + 127.0.0.1, then Save scope.Rename project Change the display name (must be unique). Filter defaults Hide static / browser noise / CDN / in-scope only by default for new proxy sessions (saved in your browser). Upstream & TLS pass-through Optional upstream proxy and hosts tunneled without certificate interception. Danger zoneType the project name to confirm, then Delete project. Removes history, map and chat for that project.

heading: Proxy & gateway
text: Listener defaults, lab browser, CA certificate and proxy options.Proxy & gatewayconfigures the listener, lab browser and CA. Start and stop the gateway from the top-bar Proxy control as well. Section What you set Listener defaultsListen host and port (default port 8088). Check portsees if it's free.Lab browserProxy modeOff / Optional / Required, browser pick, Open lab Chromium, Stop listener, Reset.Active gateway Status and address of the running listener. PentAgent CA certificateDownload CA certificate(pentagent-ca-cert.crt). Lab Chromium trusts it automatically; download for manual setups.Proxy options Upstream proxy chain and TLS pass-through hosts (no MITM). Restart the listener after changes.

heading: Collaborator
text: Generate out-of-band payloads and watch HTTP and DNS callbacks.Collaboratoris a local out-of-band listener (HTTP + DNS). Generate a payload, put it somewhere that might trigger a blind callback (SSRF, XXE, XSS beacon), then watch Interactions.

heading: Start the listener
text: The status at the top shows Listener runningor Listener stopped, with the HTTP and DNS ports. Start or stop it from here or from Settings › Collaborator. Host and ports come from server environment variables (defaults: 127.0.0.1, HTTP 8099, DNS 5300, domain oast.pentagent.local). Restart the API after changing them.

heading: Generate a payload
text: Choose HTTP or DNS Then click Generate. Copy or insert Copy payload, or Insert into Repeater/ Insert into Intruder. Or use Insert payload into Repeaterto put it into a URL query, an X-Collaboratorheader, or the body. Use a lab snippet Copyable lab snippetsgive you ready curl/ digcommands against the local listener.

heading: Interactions
text: Filter by protocol (All/ HTTP only/ DNS only) and search detail / path / from. Tick Auto-refreshor click Refresh now. Export with Export CSVor Export JSON.

heading: Comparer
text: Diff two requests or responses side by side.Comparershows what’s different between two messages. Right-click a request elsewhere and choose Send to Comparer, or switch a side to Pasteand paste text.

heading: Compare two items
text: Pick A and B Choose a transaction for each side, or switch to Pasteand paste into Paste item A…/ Paste item B…. Choose what to diff Response, Requestor Both. Choose how to tokenise Words (token diff), Lines, or Bytes (hex). Tick Ignore whitespaceto skip whitespace-only differences (not available in Bytes mode). Compare Press Compare. Removals from A and additions in B are highlighted.

heading: Decoder
text: Encode, decode and hash values, or chain several steps together.Decoderturns text between formats. Paste or type into the input, then encode or decode.

heading: Encode and decode
text: The Encode and Decode lists cover URL, Base64, Base64URL, Hex, ASCII hex, Unicode escapes, HTML, Gzip (b64) and Deflate (b64), among others. Smart decodetries common formats for you. JWT decodesplits a token into Header, Payload and Signature (it doesn't verify the signature). Hashcovers MD5, SHA-1 and SHA-256. Switch between Textand Hexviews. Use as input ←loads the current output back into the input.

heading: Chain
text: Build a pipeline: click + step, pick an operation for each step, then Run chain. Clear chainremoves every step. Results land in the Workspace; click one to load it as input, or Clear workspaceto wipe them.

heading: Send the result on
text: Send output → Intruder bodyloads the output into the Intruder request body.Send output → Intruder payloadsloads each output line into Intruder payload set 1.

heading: Inspector
text: See params, cookies and headers for the message you have selected.Inspectoris the side panel on the right of the workbench, not a top-level tab. When you select a message in Proxy, History, Organizer or elsewhere, it lists that message’s params, cookies and headers.

heading: Use the Inspector
text: Toggle it with the Inspector shortcut (see Shortcuts).Switch between Requestand Response.Edit name/value pairs and click + addfor a new one. Form body params appear under Body params (form).Open in Repeater with changessends the edited query, headers, cookies and form body to a new Repeater tab. With nothing selected, it says Select a message to inspect params, cookies, and headers.

heading: Intruder
text: Send one request many times, swapping in a list of values at the places you mark.Intrudertakes one request, marks spots with §…§, and replaces those spots with values from a payload set. Use it to try many inputs quickly.

heading: Start an attack
text: Load a request Send a request from History, Target, Decoder or elsewhere, or paste one into Intruder. Mark positions Select text in the URL, headers or body and click Add payload position, press, or use the right-click menu. Positions look like?id=§1§or /api/§FUZZ§. Build a payload set Choose a type (Simple list, File / wordlist, Numbers, Brute forcer, Dates, Null payloads, Usernamesor Case substitution), then paste values or load a wordlist file. Start Click Start attackor press. Stopends it early. Shortcuts on this tab: start/stop, save the config, add a position.

heading: Payload sets and processors
text: You can have several sets. Click + Setfor another. For each set, Processorschange every value before it is sent. Available processors include Prefix, Suffix, URL-encode / decode, Base64 / Base64URL / Base64 decode, HTML-encode, MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, Reverse and Skip (match).

heading: Attack options
text: Option What it does Follow redirects Follow 3xx responses. Max requests Hard stop after this many sends. Concurrent requests How many to send at once. Delay (ms) Pause between sends. Grep — Extract Pull a value out of each response with a named regex capture group. Grep — Match Flag responses that contain a needle (plain text, or regex if you confirm).

heading: Results
text: Results fill a table as they arrive. Use Filter results…to narrow them, and Export CSVto save them. Click a row to inspect it; double-click to send it to Repeater. From a row you can also Send to Chator Send to Organizer. Saveand Load…keep attack configs so you can rerun them later.

heading: Organizer
text: Keep interesting requests in collections with notes, tags and leads.Organizeris where you park requests worth coming back to. Right-click any request elsewhere and choose Send to Organizer, or press the Organizer shortcut from a selected message.

heading: Collections
text: Items live in collections. Create one with New collection. Open an item to set a status ( To do, In review, Won't fixand others), a highlight colour, tags and notes. Notes autosave; press to focus the notes box and to save. Move →and Copy to…put the item into another collection. Params, cookies and headers for the selected item show in the Inspector on the right.

heading: Search and filters
text: Control What it does Search notes, tags, host, path… Finds items across collections. All statuses Narrow by status. All items / Has AI lead / Open leads Show only items with an AI lead, or open leads. Tag filter Match a tag substring. Export CSV / Export JSON Download the current view.

heading: AI leads
text: When Scanner or Agent queues a lead, it lands here with an AI Leadfield. Fill in Lead statusand notes for later Plan work — leads are pivots for a later plan, not a mid-campaign replan.

heading: Repeater
text: Edit a request by hand, send it again, and compare what comes back.Repeateris for trying one request over and over with small changes. Each request gets its own tab, so you can keep several experiments going at once.

heading: Open a request in Repeater
text: In HTTP history, click the Send to Repeaterarrow, or right-click a row and send it.Double-click a row in Intruder results, the Target sitemap, or other tables that say Double-click to send to Repeater.From the Inspector, click Open in Repeater with changes.Or paste a raw request into an empty tab.With nothing open yet, Repeater says Send to Repeater from History or paste a request.

heading: Work with tabs
text: To Do this Open a new tab +or Rename a tab Double-click its name. Close a tab The ×on the tab. See what this tab sent before ◀ History, the per-tab send history.

heading: Send the request
text: Edit the request Change anything in the request editor: method, path, headers or body. Send it Click Sendor press. The response appears next to the request. If the site redirects and Follow redirectsis on, the redirect chain is shown as well.

heading: Send options
text: Option What it does Follow redirects Follow 3xx responses to the final page. Via proxyAutosends through the project listener when capture is running. Requirealways uses it, and Directskips it.Send as:Send as a saved principal (a signed-in user). This replaces the Cookie and Authorization headers. draft headerssends exactly what you typed.Send w/o CLSend without updating Content-Length ().Send ×N Send several identical requests at the same moment, to check how the site handles a race. WebSocket Switch the tab to WebSocket messages. Parent trafficjumps back to the captured request this tab came from. Repeater sends real requests to the target. Only use it on systems you’re allowed to test.

heading: Scanner
text: Run a passive audit on captured traffic and review the issues it finds.Scannerlooks through traffic you’ve already captured and flags possible issues. It doesn’t send new attacks on its own. Issues are identification leads. Confirmed findings with evidence show up under Records → Findings.

heading: Run a passive scan
text: Capture some traffic Browse your target in the lab window first. Start the scan Click New passive scan(or Run a passive scanwhen the list is empty). You can also start one from the Dashboard. While it runs, the status shows on the Dashboard. When it finishes, issues appear here. Tick Group by ruleto group them. Open Dashboardjumps back to the live overview.

heading: Review an issue
text: Select an issue to see its severity, host and evidence. From there you can Open evidence in HTTP history, View transaction, View in Target / History, or Open in Records. Passive scans only look at what you’ve already captured. Queue AI leads (when enabled) sends candidates to Organizer under the Has AI leadfilter.

heading: Sequencer
text: Capture session tokens and check whether they look random.Sequencercollects session tokens and runs statistical checks on them. A PASS means the sample looks reasonably random under these checks. A FAIL means entropy, uniformity or sample size looks weak. This is a signal, not a security proof.

heading: Live capture
text: Pick a source Choose a Source transactionthat returns a cookie or token, then click Use selected. Set Token location Set-Cookie, Response body (regex)or Response header. Fill in the cookie name, header name, or a regex with a capture group. Preview extractionshows what would be pulled. Start capture Click Start capture. Aim for at least 100 samples. Stopends it. Then click Analyze.

heading: Manual paste
text: Switch to Manual paste, paste one token per line, and click Analyze pasted samples. Fewer than 100 samples may be unreliable.

heading: What the analysis shows
text: Check What it means Effective entropy How unpredictable each character looks. Higher is better; about 3.0 bits/char is treated as a minimum for session-like tokens. Chi-square Whether characters appear about equally often. A high score suggests bias. Monobit Whether 0s and 1s are balanced in the bit stream. Runs How often the bit stream flips. Too few or too many suggests correlation. Uniqueness How many unique tokens vs total. Heavy repetition usually means a short pool. Length / character distribution How sizes and characters vary. Send token source to Repeateropens the source request for more digging. The sample table lists every captured token; duplicates are highlighted.

heading: Target & scope
text: Set which hosts are in scope, and browse the sitemap of what you've captured.The Targettab has two jobs: deciding which hosts are in scope for this project, and showing a sitemap of the URLs you’ve captured.

heading: Scope
text: Scope is a list of include and exclude rules. A URL is in scope when it matches an Includerule and no Excluderule. Host accepts host:portor host/#/for an SPA. Path prefix narrows it (for example /api). Leave Path prefix blank for the whole origin. Empty includes mean all hosts match until excludes apply. Add rules Click + Add ruleunder Include or Exclude. Fill in Hostand optionally Path prefix. Save Click Save scopeor press. Check a URL Paste a URL into Check URL against scope. The result is In scopeor Out of scope, and it tests the rules you see right now — you don’t have to save first. Unsaved scope changes If you leave the tab with edits you haven’t saved, PentAgent asks whether to Save, Discardor Cancel. You can also edit scope under Settings › Project, including templates like localhost + 127.0.0.1.

heading: Sitemap
text: The sitemap fills as you browse through the proxy. Use In-scope only, Hide staticand Search path…to narrow it. Collapse all/ Expand alland Refreshcontrol the tree. Click an endpoint to see methods and parameters in Endpoint detail. Double-click to send it to Repeater. Right-click for Add to scope, Filter History, Send to Repeater, Send to Chator Send to Organizer. Seeing an empty tree? Browse your target in the lab window first. The empty state points you to the Proxy tab.
